title: The marquee answers to M
goal: Every other tool has a letter, and the marquee, which is the tool the copy and fill commands are built around, has none: you have to reach for the tool bar with the mouse every time. M is what Photoshop uses for it and pressing it again should swap between the box and the ellipse.
notes: Tool.shortcutKey in Sources/PhotonzCore/Tools.swift returns nil for rectSelect and ellipseSelect although the comment on isMarqueeSelectTool already calls them Photoshop's M group. Tool groups already cycle on a repeated press elsewhere (toolGroupsFlag). RESOLVED: the marquee already answered to M (the letter lives on ToolGroup.selection.groupKey, not on Tool.shortcutKey, which is why the source read as if it had none). The work was the second press, plus stopping M from handing over the wand.
acceptance: Pressing M picks the rectangular marquee
Pressing M again swaps to the ellipse marquee, and again back
The tool bar tooltip shows the key, the way the other tools do

log.note: Adversarial review before building, on the running probe rather than on the source. The task's premise was half wrong: M already picked the marquee. A probe walk from the arrow tool gave rectSelect on the first press and rectSelect again on the second and third, so only the swap was missing. The tooltip already printed M as well.

Also found: M could hand you the MAGIC WAND. The selection slot's letter picked the remembered member, and the wand is a member, so W then M gave the wand back. M is Photoshop's marquee and the wand has W of its own, so M now always hands over a marquee.

Model, in PhotonzCore (TDD, 6 new tests): ToolGroup.tools(answeringTo:) gives the members a plain letter owns (its own letter owns one tool; the family letter owns the members with no letter, which is exactly the marquee pair), and tool(forKey:active:remembered:) resolves a press: already holding one of the letter's tools moves on to the next, otherwise the remembered member when the letter owns it, else the letter's first. So O is still always Ellipse and only M swaps.

App: ToolGroupShortcuts now asks for the tool at the moment of the press (pick(key)) instead of baking one in at build time; ToolGroupButton teaches the swap in its tooltip and at the foot of its flyout; the overflow stand-ins no longer register the marquee slot's own M on top of the family's, which would have left one of the two answering.

Verified on the probe: new walks marquee-answers-to-m-walk.json (M, M, M walks box, ellipse, box; tooltip capture reads "Rectangle Select M"; W then M gives a marquee) and marquee-m-narrow-walk.json (the same on the compact bar). tool-bar-families.json rewritten for the new selection rules and green. current-selection-slot, tool-bar-feedback, shift-letter-shortcut and frame-name-rename walks all still pass. Scripts/test.sh: 4645 tests green.

Acceptance: (1) M picks the rectangular marquee, verified live. (2) M again swaps to the ellipse and again back, verified live and in the model tests. (3) The tooltip reads "Rectangle Select M", verified on a real screen capture. (4) Nothing displaced: no new key was registered at all, and no menu item anywhere in the bar carries a plain M.
Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-08-marquee-answers-to-m.json with two real window captures.

M swaps the marquee: pressing it hands over the rectangular marquee from any tool and pressing it again swaps the box for the ellipse and back, and M no longer hands over the magic wand (which keeps W). Model in PhotonzCore (ToolGroup.tools(answeringTo:) and tool(forKey:active:remembered:), tests first); the bar's key stand-ins now resolve a press live, and the tooltip and flyout teach the swap. Next only. Verified on the probe with marquee-answers-to-m-walk, marquee-m-narrow-walk and the rewritten tool-bar-families walk, plus Scripts/test.sh (4645 green).
